summary.headline: Max India consolidated revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR95.5 crore in Q2 FY27 while EBITDA loss halved to INR11.4 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR95.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 90.4% YoY and 40% QoQ from INR68.6 crore in Q1. EBITDA loss narrowed to INR11.4 crore from INR25.3 crore a year earlier and INR24.9 crore in Q1, a 55% YoY and 54% QoQ reduction. Noida Antara handovers passed 200 of 340 units, with management guiding AGEasy EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and Care Homes breakeven by end-H1 FY28. Management also flagged a possible restructuring of the three businesses, with no details yet.

segments.name: Assisted Care Services (Antara Senior Living residences)
segments.commentary: Noida handovers exceeded 200 of 340 units, with Phase 1 revenue recognised for 131 units; Estate 360 sold out, and Estate 361 has 263 of 360 units sold. Revenue is lumpy and tied to construction-linked collections, with DM fee at 9.5% of collections.

segments.name: Care Homes
segments.commentary: Care Home Services revenue INR12.28 crore (+40% YoY). Occupancy across all beds rose to 29% from 26% QoQ, across 485 beds, and four of eight homes are at or above plan.

segments.name: AGEasy
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR35 crore; September was the highest monthly revenue at INR14.9 crore, implying exit ARR near INR180 crore. ROAS improved to 4.7 from 2 in Q1, and online D2C and marketplace gross margin held at 45%.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy to reach EBITDA breakeven and marginally positive in Q4 FY27; CM2 trending toward zero (11% in September).
Care Homes expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of H1 FY28; company expects positivity across businesses in H2 FY28.
Noida Phase 2 IRR expected at 15-17% on the basis of current market pricing of about INR18,000 per sq ft versus INR6,500-7,000 for Phase 1 sales.

New pipeline: Bengaluru (6.5 lakh sq ft, potential sales value about INR900 crore, pure DM model), Dehradun (INR850-900 crore), plus Delhi NCR and one South India project. Management reiterated INR1,800 crore annual gross sales value commitment.
Noida Phase 1 handovers expected to finish by end of November 2026; maintenance charges start 1 November 2026.
capex_capacity: Care Homes: 485 beds in operation; each home takes about 4 quarters to reach 40-45% occupancy (unit-level CM positive) and 8-10 quarters to reach 60% maturity, at which point unit CM is 30-32% and EBITDA after HO cost is 16-18%.

Noida Antara: community fully operational; 200+ of 340 units handed over; Phase 2 building plan revalidation awaits Noida Authority acceptance of the sports-sector resolution plan submitted by the lead developer.
Estate 361: 180 units launched Dec 2025 and 180 in June 2026; about 97 units remaining unsold.
Management stated Phase 2 expenses are held in inventory, and only Phase 1 Tower 1-3 project costs are expensed, so no loss was booked in Q2.
demand_pricing: Care Homes ARPOB averaged about INR6,900 in Q2 (from INR5,800 six quarters ago); fresh move-ins in September 2026 reached about INR8,400. Management aspires to about INR9,000 within 12 months.
Care Homes occupancy ranges 16-40% by home in H1; individual homes at 45-55% in September exit. Old-bed occupancy rose to 36% from 21%.
AGEasy marketing efficiency (ROAS) at 4.7; brand searches up over 50% and direct traffic more than doubled between April and August 2026. Gross margins pressured by Middle East logistics costs.
Dehradun community stable with 3 units re-released in Q2, generating about INR2 crore of marketing fee; satisfaction index 89%.
Noida Phase 1 sales cited at INR6,500-7,000 per unit price; current market for Phase 2 cited at about INR18,000.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the AGEasy Q2 surge is seasonal versus sustainable, and why did offline revenue jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishaan Khanna said 75-80% of the surge is sustainable, with some rationalisation expected in October; Q3 is expected to beat Q2. Offline growth came from expanded distributor networks built over three quarters, with more geographies to open.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise, and when will they stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta attributed the rise to 150+ hires for Noida plus unanticipated labour code and PF regulation changes. Ajay Agrawal said corporate employee cost is stable and future increases will be tied to new projects, geographies and care homes.

qa_highlights.question: How is the ASL DM fee recognised: at collection or completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Agrawal said the fee is recognised on collections made by Max Estates, reconciled quarterly, at 9.5% less pass-through and brokerage, so it accrues in real time rather than at project completion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state ARPOB for Care Homes?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta said annual revenue per bed is INR22-25 lakh; Ishaan Khanna said the 12-month aspiration is about INR9,000 per day, rising with clinical cross-sell and upsell.

qa_highlights.question: What were the finance lease and treasury income figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Agrawal said finance lease income was about INR15 crore, similar to Q1. Residences other income was INR10.7 crore, of which INR2.7 crore is eliminated, leaving INR8 crore from treasury and loans to JV Contend.

qa_highlights.question: How much DM fee was recognised from Noida and why no loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Agrawal said Noida DM fee was INR9.98 crore for the half year (INR33 lakh in June, the rest in September). Phase 2 costs are held in inventory, so only Phase 1 costs are expensed and the result is a marginal gain.

qa_highlights.question: Will AGEasy be demerged, and when does the business turn EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta said restructuring thoughts are under consideration across governance and investor-reach lines but are premature. AGEasy is expected to break even in Q4 FY27 and Care Homes by end-H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Care Homes unit-level breakeven model?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta said each home takes about 4 quarters to reach 40-45% occupancy, when unit CM turns positive, and 8-10 quarters to reach 60% maturity with 30-32% unit CM and 16-18% EBITDA after HO cost.

risks_watch: Revenue and DM fee are lumpy, tied to construction milestones and collections, so quarterly consolidated EBITDA may swing; management says the residences business is EBITDA positive over the project cycle.
AGEasy gross margins are under pressure from Middle East logistics costs; the CM2 breakeven target of Q4 FY27 depends on sustaining the monthly run rate after the festive season.
Noida Phase 2 timing depends on Noida Authority accepting the resolution plan and on the building plan revalidation, with 2-3 customers awaiting bank approvals.
Employee costs are rising due to labour code and PF changes and new hires, which could pressure margins until projects scale.
Possible restructuring or demerger of the three businesses is under consideration, with no details or timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on top-line growth and loss reduction, with specific numbers on each vertical. Cautious and evasive on the restructuring question, calling it premature, and on consolidated breakeven timing, which it ties to vertical-level milestones.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA loss cut to INR11.4 crore from INR24.9 crore in Q1 (-54% QoQ), with AGEasy EBITDA breakeven guided for Q4 FY27 and Care Homes breakeven by end-H1 FY28; CM2 for AGEasy at 29% and Care Homes at 63%, though employee costs are rising from 150+ Noida hires and labour code changes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Noida Phase 2 (340-unit Antara tower set) depends on Noida Authority accepting the resolution plan and building plan revalidation, and Care Homes stays at 485 beds with occupancy only 29%, so no new capacity is commissioned in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Care Home occupancy rose to 29% from 26% QoQ across 485 beds, AGEasy Q2 net revenue INR35 crore (1.9x QoQ) with September at INR14.9 crore implying exit ARR near INR180 crore, and Noida handovers passed 200 of 340 units with Phase 1 completion by end-November 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed directly; the business is asset-light DM/management-fee led, with Noida Phase 2 costs held in inventory and a new pipeline (Bengaluru 6.5 lakh sq ft, Dehradun INR850-900 crore) that could require project-level funding, though Max India treasury assets are INR52 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated INR1,800 crore annual gross sales value and says it will be 'more than met' for the next few years, with Q3 expected to beat Q2 for AGEasy, but no quantified revenue upgrade has been given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue and DM fees are lumpy and tied to collections, AGEasy gross margin is pressured by Middle East logistics costs, and AGEasy CM2 fell to 11% in September from 18.5% in Q1 (48% earlier), so the Q4 FY27 breakeven depends on sustaining the monthly run rate after the festive season.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New pipeline projects (Bengaluru 6.5 lakh sq ft at about INR900 crore potential sales value, Dehradun INR850-900 crore, Delhi NCR and one South India project) could be launched, but timing is not given and no product launch date was named.

rows.label: AGEasy EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management guided AGEasy to EBITDA breakeven and marginally positive in Q4 FY27, with CM2 at 11% in September and Q2 net revenue INR35 crore (1.7x YoY), but gross margin is under pressure from Middle East logistics costs.
